## Notes from the translator

* `Minecraft.getInstance()` became `compat::minecraft()`: the Minecraft the game hands its tick events, recorded on the first client tick (it panics if called before that)
* native field names are the Mojang names in snake_case - check them against the port
* a game object's `minecraft` field became `compat::minecraft()` (Java sets it to the one Minecraft)
* `==` on two objects is IDENTITY in Java; it became `std::ptr::eq` - check the call sites that compare values
* an anonymous class with one method became a closure - where the port expects a trait object, wrap it in a struct implementing that trait
* a Java `throw` became a `panic!` (a checked exception in Java is an unwinding panic here; `catch` blocks are `std::panic::catch_unwind`)
* a port method that returns `Result` is `.unwrap()`ed where Java would throw
* Text/Component.translatable(key): SeerClient script text is plain - the KEY is shown; put the English text in, or look it up yourself
* `super.mouseClicked(..)` & co in a mod screen answer `false`: the game's widget pass runs after an override that answers false (the port's `super` body), not before its own code
* `super.extractRenderState(..)` in a mod screen: the game draws the background and the widgets before the override runs (MODDING.md "Mod screens")
* a screen's / widget's `font` became `compat::font()` (`Screen.init` sets it to `minecraft.font`)
* Java arguments that are the frame's context (a GuiGraphics, a Font, the Minecraft) are dropped where the port takes `&Gl` / the Minecraft itself
* port methods that take the frame's `&Gl` / the `Minecraft` get `gl_state_manager::gl()` / `compat::minecraft()`
* `setScreen(parent)` became `game::set_screen_to_parent()` - the port holds the screen a mod screen was opened over (`set_screen_keeping_parent`)
* several `catch` clauses became one `if let Err(..)` (a panic has no exception type to match on): the first clause's body runs
* a game object's `font` became `compat::font()` (the port's `Font` view over the font set)
* `CompletableFuture.supplyAsync(.., executor)`: the Java executor became `compat::executor` (a new thread per task)
* ScreenKeyboardEvents.afterKeyPress(screen) is per-screen in Fabric and GLOBAL in SeerClient: the listener now sees every screen - test the screen's type in it
* `Integer.parseInt` & co became `str::parse().expect(..)`: a bad number panics where Java throws NumberFormatException (a surrounding `catch` is `catch_unwind`)
* ScreenKeyboardEvents.allowKeyPress(screen) is per-screen in Fabric and GLOBAL in SeerClient: the listener now sees every screen - test the screen's type in it
* a Java downcast `(T) x` became `x.as_any().downcast_ref::<T>().unwrap()` (a failed cast panics, as Java throws ClassCastException)
* ScreenMouseEvents.allowMouseClick(screen) is per-screen in Fabric and GLOBAL in SeerClient: the listener now sees every screen - test the screen's type in it
* `super.mouseClicked(..)` & co in a mod container screen answer `false`: the base screen's handling runs after an override that answers false
* some game fields the mod reads are private in the port - make them `pub` or use the port's accessor (the compiler names them)
* HudElementRegistry.attachElementAfter: the element is drawn after the vanilla HUD (HudRenderCallback) - its position in the layer order is not kept
* nested sub-commands under `hud` were not ported
* a call on a `ChestMenu` the mod kept reads the open menu while it is still that one (`compat::LiveChestMenu::with`; `None` once the server closed it - Java reads the closed object)
* HudElementRegistry.attachElementBefore: the element is drawn after the vanilla HUD (HudRenderCallback) - its position in the layer order is not kept
* nested sub-commands under `custom` were not ported
* a command argument (`argument(..)`) became words in `ctx.args` - read and parse them by hand
* `.requires(..)` was dropped

## Next steps

1. `seer check` (tools/seer, MODDING.md section 23) re-validates the manifest and every hook target with the game's own rules.
1. Build the game as the SDK build (MODDING.md section 7), then `cargo build --release` here - the compiler will point at every snake_case guess that does not match the port.
1. `seer pack` (or the generated `py pack.py`) packs the DLL, the manifest and the resources.
1. `py tools/hook_coverage.py --class <Class>` says whether a target that is not hooked yet has a Rust body (PORTED - ask for a hook) or none (NO RUST).
